title: offer-negotiation-and-evidence-based-comp-guidance-2026
author: Priya Malhotra
body:
Summary:
This guide explains Redwood's recommended approach for offer conversations, manager negotiation cadence, and the evidence required to approve exceptions to published compensation bands. It is written for hiring managers and people-ops partners who are operating within our PLG-led hiring funnel and need to close offers quickly while preserving internal equity and auditability.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to all full-time and long-term contractor offer decisions made by hiring managers in North America and Europe.
- Does NOT supplant legal review for international tax/immigration clauses, nor special enterprise-customer sign-on incentives (refer to Finance & Legal).
- Purpose: accelerate decision-making, reduce offer cycles, and create auditable compensation decisions with clear business justification.

Key principles (short):
1) Evidence-first: Every offer above midpoint of band requires at least two documented data points (market comp data, internal benchmark, or demonstrable business impact).
2) Manager accountability: Hiring manager owns initial offer strategy; people-ops owns approval and audit.
3) Speed with guardrails: 48-hour SLA on approvals for standard offers; 72–96 hours for comp-exceptions.

Pre-offer checklist (Manager):
1. Confirm role band and level using Compensation Bands doc.
2. Document candidate target in ATS with: current comp, target comp, sign-on needs, relocation, and preferred start date.
3. Capture 2 supporting evidence artifacts (select at least two):
   - Market benchmark snapshot (Radford, levels.fyi, external recruiter comps)
   - Internal comparator evidence (names of 1–2 recent hires at same band + hire dates and onsite summaries)
   - Unique candidate outcome evidence (e.g., published patents, shipped feature with metrics, prior revenue/ARR linked to role)
4. Early people-ops sync: Drop a 30-minute slot in People-ops intake channel with docs attached.

Offer structure recommendations (standard template):
- Base salary (annual)
- Target bonus / variable comp (if applicable)
- Equity grant: grant size, expected vesting schedule, refresh eligibility note
- Sign-on bonus (one-time): amount and payment timing
- Relocation or work-authorization support (if applicable)
- Start date and probation period highlights

Manager negotiation script (concise, for live or email):
- Positive open: "We're excited about your skills — we think you'll add X to our team in the first 90 days."
- Offer summary: "The proposed package is..." (list components succinctly).
- If counter: "We evaluated market data and internal precedents. Here are two reasons we landed here..."
- If candidate requests more: "I hear that. To request an adjustment, I'll need one or more of these: 1) competing offer docs; 2) evidence of materially different responsibilities; 3) a short summary of business impact the candidate will drive. I'll get back within 72 hours."

Escalation & approval workflow (people-ops + manager):
1. Standard offer (within band midpoint or below): Manager issues offer; people-ops notified via ATS for audit. Approval SLA: 48 hours.
2. Near-band top (between midpoint and top): Manager must attach evidence checklist and people-ops signs off. Approval SLA: 48–72 hours.
3. Above-band/top or outlier total comp (>15% above top of band or large equity deviation): People-ops requires executive compensation sign-off (Head of People or Finance), written justification with evidence, and a calibrated review meeting. Approval SLA: 72–96 hours.
4. Special cases (counteroffers, relocation packages above guideline, or candidate-requested guaranteed bonuses): Legal and Finance routing required; expect longer lead time.

Required evidence matrix (for exceptions):
- Exception type: External competitive offer 
  - Required evidence: full competing offer document (redacted as needed), recruiter confirmation, and market benchmark 
- Exception type: Role scope misalignment with band 
  - Required evidence: updated job packet, peer comparator list, and hiring manager written justification (150–300 words)
- Exception type: Critical hire for product or revenue impact 
  - Required evidence: product/CS/BD owner email with measurable OKR/impact and a 30/60/90 plan

Audit & recordkeeping:
- People-ops will attach the compensation decision record to the ATS candidate record and the central comp-exceptions spreadsheet (retained 7 years).
- All approvals must be captured as a signed email thread or approval in the HRIS approval flow.
- Redacted evidence may be saved for future calibration sessions.

Manager templates (copy/paste):
- Offer email subject: "Redwood | Offer: [Role] — [Candidate Name]"
- Offer email body (short):
  "Hi [Candidate],

  We're excited to offer you the [Role] on the [Team]. Below is the summary of your offer: 
  - Base: $[base]
  - Bonus target: [X%] of base
  - Equity: [grant, vesting]
  - Sign-on: $[amount] (if applicable)

  This is a formal offer contingent on standard background checks. Please let me know if you'd like to discuss. We request a decision by [date].

  Best,
  [Hiring Manager]"

People-ops intake form (fields to copy into ATS notes):
- Candidate name, role, band, proposed comp, candidate current comp, additional ask amount, evidence links (market/internal/comparators), business-impact note, manager name, proposed start date, hiring manager ETA for response.

Common negotiation scenarios and recommended responses:
1. Candidate asks for higher equity because of anticipated future value: Explain our refresh cadence and grant philosophy; offer a targeted performance-linked milestone for a mid-year review if appropriate.
2. Competing cash offer materially higher: Request proof of offer; evaluate whether this hire is mission-critical and whether an exception is warranted.
3. Senior hire asking for above-band salary for retention from current employer: Validate retention risk and document the business impact. Consider limited sign-on tied to 6–12 month retention clause.

Operating metrics and SLAs to monitor (people-ops):
- Time from verbal acceptance to written offer: target <24 hours for standard offers.
- Approval SLA adherence: 95% within stated SLAs.
- Offer acceptance rate by band and role: tracked monthly; escalate negative trends to Head of Talent.

Training and calibration cadence for managers:
- Quarterly 45-minute calibration sessions run by People-ops covering 10 recent offers (redacted) with comparative evidence.
- Annual comp-band refresh workshops with Finance to update midpoint/top guidelines.

Appendix A — Example justification snippet (150 words):
"Candidate X commanded a lead engineering position at a competitor where they led delivery of a low-latency feature that improved retention by 8% and enabled $3M incremental ARR. We have two internal comparators hired in the last 12 months at the same level whose profiles and responsibilities align closely; market benchmarking from two vendors supports a proposal 12% above midpoint. Given the role is critical to Q3 roadmap delivery and the quantified business impact, we request an above-band base with a conditional 6-month performance review for a staged equity refresh."

Appendix B — Legal & regional considerations:
- EU hires: Include gross-to-net guidance specific to country. Work with Finance on tax gross-up only if pre-approved.
- Relocation and immigration: Offer contingencies must be explicit; coordinate with Ops and Legal for timelines.

Questions, exceptions, or requests for a calibration review should be directed to people-ops@example.redwood.com.

Document ownership and revision history:
- Owner: People-ops (Comp & Offer Operations)
- Next scheduled review: 2027-01-15
- Revision notes: 2026-03-02 — published initial People-ops approved version.
